paragraphs.text: The 30th Anniversary Edition of Beta is a commemorative , collectible , non-tournament-legal card set celebrating thirty years of Magic . The set was released on November 28, 2022 and sold through 30thEdition.wizards.com . The sale was "concluded" after 40 minutes.

Inspired by Limited Edition Beta , 30th Anniversary Edition aimed to let collectors experience elements of Magic's early years. Each display of 30th Anniversary Edition contained four booster packs with random content for $ 999.-. This made it the most expensive official Magic product to date. These collectible cards had a different card back and were therefore not legal in any sanctioned Magic event. For the same reason, it didn't violate the Reserved List . The set had a limited print run.

Each booster pack contained 15 cards, 13 cards in the modern frame — 1 rare, 3 uncommons, 7 commons, and 2 basic lands — plus one basic land in the retro frame , one additional retro frame card, and a token . Approximately three out of every ten packs contained a rare retro frame card. Each card used a special Black Lotus inspired card back rather than the standard Deckmaster back. The cards in the set were numbered #-1-594 (297 modern frame, 297 retro frame).

Nearly every card included matched the rarity of its counterpart in Beta . There were no mythic rares , and almost all rarities had stayed the same. These cards did, however, have modern wording and modern corners, and some of the art had been touched up. The retro frame was the same frame used in Time Spiral Remastered . Returning features were the original white mana symbol , the original basic land template, and the classic art .

Players were upset about the release. Complaints were uttered about the price range, the targeting of high-spending players instead of the common player base, the random packaging, the perceived violation of the Reserved List , and Wizards' hypocritical sale of proxies .
On November 14, 2022, a Bank of America analyst called out the 30th Anniversary Edition as particularly egregious, though their assessment and motivations were contrary to community criticisms.

Meanwhile, Quinton Hoover 's estate alleged that Wizards of the Coast was using his art without permission and that they did not have the rights to do so. Jesper Myrfors complained that his name was unjustly removed of the copyright notice from the card.

In January 2026, a lawsuit filed by shareholders against the company and its directors alleged that Hasbro had overproduced Magic cards in 2021-2023, propping up short-term results but destroying the long-term value of the brand. 30th Anniversary Edition was cited as an example. According to testimony from several members of leadership shared in the complaint, Hasbro management had made a plan to pause sales of the set if it would become apparent that they were weaker than anticipated. The company announced that the sale had concluded, and the product was unavailable for further purchases, effectively making it look like the product was far more popular than it actually had been.
